raw_response:
I am old now, but I still farm the same 3 mu myself with my family. We do wheat and then maize, same as around here. I do not like making big changes. Land this small cannot take much risk. If wheat is done well, then maize can follow right away, so I keep the usual wheat-maize rotation. I will not buy fancy seed or put too much fertilizer, because fertilizer and water both cost money, but I also do not dare use too little and lose yield. For wheat, I will put base fertilizer before sowing, then add a bit more when it turns green after winter. I will water a few times if the sky stays dry, especially after sowing and around jointing. For maize, the time is tight after wheat harvest, so I will clear the field quickly, do simple tillage, sow fast, and use one base dose plus one topdressing. I spray only if I really see weeds or insects. My plan is to keep things steady, spend carefully, and make sure both crops give grain.
